Ran into this and wanted to add a pretty significant issue this causes with Plex. 

Plex analyzes each media file when added to its library. This is needed to ensure when files are streamed, Plex has all the data about the file, including duration. If this error occurs she Plex is analyzing a file, that data will be incomplete / corrupt and will cause playback issues. 

Had this happen to a file I added. Plex would think the duration was less than it really was, causing buffering and playback issues. When I manually forced Plex to re-analyze the affected file, the issues disappeared. 

I know this doesn't add anything helpful but just wanted to raise the impact that it can corrupt items in your Plex library and you can't know which ones until you play them back, hit some playback issues and re-analyze the file.

http://beta.rclone.org/v1.34-62-gec0916c/ (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

> crypt: return unexpected EOF instead of Failed to authenticate decrypted block
> 
> Streams which truncated early with an EOF message would return a
> "Failed to authenticate decrypted block" error.  While technically
> correct, this isn't a helpful error message as it masks the underlying
> problem.  This changes it to return "unexpected EOF" instead.

The rest of rclone knows it should retry such errors.
